design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. Dwayne asks only how much it takes to get his PrePay meter back on and to pay it. The scored root is the restore payment (56.8): restore target less prepaid balance plus a cushion. The restore rule carries two prerequisite sentences, both in the negated direction: the quote is not given until the prepaid balance carries the meter error refund for every fast meter test (state form), and not before the low-balance alert amount owed a reset after the latest disconnection has been reset (action form). At frozen_time the meter test cc702350-020d-4f81-aebc-5d7ef35ad4d0 found the meter 3.80 percent fast this morning and no refund line exists, and the enrollment (b87c5de1-baa5-4216-843e-9cda2421d20d) is disconnected after three low-balance disconnections in the month with alert amount 55.00 while the reset rule gives 61. The agent must compute the refund (14.77, five factors over the prepay ledger, notifications and service meter tests), compute the alert reset (61, six factors over prepay history, service certificates and returns, and the arrangement ledger), and only then the restore payment (five factors over prepay history, service reconnect fees and pledges, and capital credits). Each policy names its own target tool in the charter (the published rule text names no tool); the difficulty is in reading rules and records.

SCOPE (task 1 of 2). Occupied by task 0: prepay_ext_postpaid_credit_carry_in and prepay_ext_activation_payment with tools post_carried_credit_69e6c97d and make_activation_payment_0416a855 (a carried-in standard-billing credit and the activation payment on an enrollment awaiting activation). Claimed here: prepay_ext_meter_error_refund (post_meter_error_refund_29b7beca, prepay_credit_adjustment with reason meter_error_refund), prepay_ext_disconnect_alert_reset (reset_low_balance_alert_c29238fa, prepay_alert_settings) and prepay_ext_restore_payment (make_restore_payment_2eb3ad28, prepay_payment on an active or disconnected enrollment with no arrears). Disjoint from task 0; the union covers all five extended policies.

DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 1): {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 5, 5]}. The alert reset takes 6 factors (1 method, 5 parameter), the meter refund 5 (2 method, 3 parameter), the restore payment 5 (1 method: assistance_pledge_cushion_method, whose tiers compute the cushion three different ways - waived, fixed charges only, days x average daily cost - and 4 parameter). Shape: fan-out; both edges value_input. Multi-source: repeat_disconnection_restore_target (notification count AND the account's alert amount) and payment_lag_warning_days (latest payment channel AND a one-month count); refunded_line_scope is not claimed as multi-source (tax and power cost adjustment sit on the same rate-schedule record). Cross-difficulty: refund window, line scope, share and test-request courtesy (service meter tests and schedule), medical/returned/arrangement warning days (service, arrange), reconnect history and pledge method (service), patronage (capital).

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root prepay_ext_restore_payment. Edge 1 -> prepay_ext_meter_error_refund: value_input, gate balance_now, form state, sentence 'The restore payment is not quoted until the prepaid balance carries the meter error refund for every meter test of the underlying service account that found the meter fast.' (ordering 'not ... until', negated direction; record-visible state: a meter-error-refund line for every fast test; no code token; closed set 'every meter test ... that found the meter fast'). Exactly one write of the difficulty books a meter error refund line: the refund rule's tool. Unresolved: initial_state.service_trouble_reports.cc702350-020d-4f81-aebc-5d7ef35ad4d0.meter_test_result = fast and no prepay_credit_adjustment row on the ledger. Flips: refund line with source the test, prepaid_balance -7.36 -> 7.41. Edge 2 -> prepay_ext_disconnect_alert_reset: value_input, gate alert_amount, form action, sentence 'The restore payment is not quoted before the low-balance alert amount owed a reset after the latest low-balance disconnection has been reset.' (negated direction 'not ... before'; names the action, never a tool). fallback_reason: the reset leaves only a number on the enrollment, which cannot show whether it is the reset for the latest disconnection (the 55.00 now on file was the reset after the 2026-09-22 disconnection). Unresolved: initial_state.prepay_accounts.b87c5de1-baa5-4216-843e-9cda2421d20d.low_balance_alert_amount = 55.0 while the rule gives 61 for the 2026-10-05 disconnection (status disconnected_low_balance, three disconnected alerts in the month). Flips: the alert amount becomes 61.0. Order: the two prerequisites touch different fields (a ledger row + prepaid_balance vs low_balance_alert_amount) and neither computation reads the other's field (the refund reads daily charge lines and notifications; the alert reset reads daily charge lines, payments, notifications and service/arrange rows), so both orders give the same terminal DB (harness: swap equal = True); gold uses refund first. Deletion sensitivity: skipping the refund gives restore payment 71.57 instead of 56.8; skipping the alert reset gives 50.8 instead of 56.8. user_scenario never names a refund, a meter test or an alert reset as something to do; its only related lines are passive reactions after the agent says so. The tools validate nothing.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. prepay_credit_adjustment: prepay_evt_enrollment_transfers (no eligibility -> policy_scope; its 'for the difference only and once per source record' sentence is retired by the declared overwrite, the refund rule keeping 'booked once for the meter test'). prepay_alert_settings: prepay_evt_alerts (no eligibility -> policy_scope; the reset stays inside low_balance_alert_min 10.00 and low_balance_alert_max 100.00: 61 is inside); prepay_evt_disconnect_reconnect read for the disconnect counts. prepay_payment: prepay_evt_activation (gates apply to prepay_activate only -> policy_scope) and prepay_evt_payment_split gate payment_limits: 56.8 within 10.00..500.00 and channel phone_ivr_card allowed; arrears_balance 0.00 so the whole payment is credited. The payment brings the balance to 64.21 >= reconnect_threshold_balance 10.00, so the system reconnects remotely afterwards (outside this tree). No time gate governs the three writes.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Refund object: meter test cc702350-020d-4f81-aebc-5d7ef35ad4d0 (fast, +3.80, resolved 2026-10-06) on service account bc97b0f3-e099-4458-b2fb-15ae384cbbde; the earlier test 342d14f0-1e4c-4c5d-b414-1731d3e8b6a3 (within tolerance, +1.10, 2026-08-28) anchors the window and the share but is not refunded. Lines included: energy and power cost adjustment lines dated 2026-09-07..2026-10-05 (window of one month); excluded: facility and program fee lines (not usage), lines 2026-08-24..2026-09-06 (before the window). Alert object: the enrollment's low_balance_alert_amount. Restore object: the enrollment; the payment row carries prepay_account_id.

FACTOR CARD - meter error refund (baseline: energy lines of a 6-month window x 3.80/103.80, both courtesies at their stated zero defaults courtesy_tests_default and courtesy_disconnects_default; baseline_result 5.67). refund_window_anchor (method): accurate test 2026-08-28 >= activation 2026-08-24 and before the fast test 2026-10-06 -> window = whole months since that test = 1; baseline 6 months gives 16.38. refunded_line_scope (parameter, multi-source): Schedule R bills PCA, no sales tax -> energy 90.72 + PCA 4.15 = 94.87; baseline energy only gives 14.67. overbilled_share_method (method): earlier error +1.10 on the fast side -> average 2.45 / 102.45; baseline 3.80/103.80 gives 15.97. test_request_courtesy (parameter): two test requests in 12 months -> 7.50; baseline 0 gives 7.27. disconnection_courtesy (parameter): three low-balance disconnections in the window (fewer than max 4) -> 5.00; baseline gives 9.77. Near-miss: the within-tolerance test is not a fast test and is never refunded. Refund = 2.27 + 7.50 + 5.00 = 14.77.

FACTOR CARD - alert reset (baseline: 3 warning days x last-month daily cost, never below 55.00; baseline_result 55.0). alert_daily_cost_window (method): activated 1 whole month ago (< 2) -> all charges since activation 218.36 / 43 days = 5.0781 instead of 130.9 / 29; baseline gives 55.0. repeat_disconnection_warning_days (parameter): 3 disconnections (more than two, fewer than 4) -> 5 days; baseline 3 gives 55.0. payment_lag_warning_days (parameter, multi-source): latest payment 2026-09-30 at a payment kiosk and 3 kiosk payments in the month -> +1; baseline gives 56. medical_certificate_warning_days (parameter, service): certificate received 2025-11-20 -> +3; baseline gives 55.0. returned_payment_warning_days (parameter, service): return 2026-05-14 -> +1; baseline gives 56. arrangement_warning_days (parameter, arrange): default rebill 2025-03-12 -> +2 (near-miss: the two missed installments would give only +1); baseline gives 55.0. 12 days x 5.0781 = 60.94 -> 61.

FACTOR CARD - restore payment (baseline: reconnect threshold 10.00 - balance, no cushion, floor 10.00; baseline_result 10.0). repeat_disconnection_restore_target (parameter, multi-source): 3 disconnections and alert 61.00 > 10.00 -> target 61.00; baseline gives 10.0. payment_frequency_cushion_days (parameter): 3 payments in the month -> 4 days; baseline gives 53.59. reconnect_history_cushion_days (parameter, service): one remote reconnect fee 2025-07-16 -> +1; baseline gives 55.73. patronage_cushion_days (parameter, capital): 30 allocation years -> -2; baseline gives 58.94. assistance_pledge_cushion_method (method, service): Operation Round Up pledge 50.00 on 2026-10-02 and no government pledge -> the cushion covers only the fixed charges, 3 days x daily_facility_charge 1.07 = 3.21 (a government pledge would waive it; no pledge would take 3 days x 4.5138 = 13.54); baseline full cushion gives 67.13. Payment = 61.00 - 7.41 + 3.21 = 56.8.

SEED ROWS AND WHY. The enrollment (activated 2026-08-24, disconnected 2026-10-05, prepaid -7.36 equal to the ledger: payments 50.00 + 42.00 + 65.00 + 30.00 + 24.00 less 218.36 of daily charges) and its full daily ledger (43 service days x facility, energy and PCA lines plus two program fees) and 14 notifications (low-balance, warning, disconnected and reconnected alerts; each disconnection on a weekday inside the window and at least 24 hours after its warning; a low-balance alert on 2026-09-24 follows the 2026-09-23 reconnection at 23.75, below the 55.00 alert amount; 2026-09-07 is Labor Day, the 2026-10-03 crossing waited for Monday). Service account Schedule R with the replacement meter; two meter tests; a medical certificate (expired before enrollment); a returned e-check with its fee and the cash payment that cleared it; a 2025 remote reconnect fee; an Operation Round Up pledge; a defaulted 2024-25 arrangement with its ledger; 30 years of capital allocations and a 2024 retirement. Every row is read by a gold finder and moves a factor or a prerequisite. Automatic clauses checked: no late charges on prepay, no counseling referral (3 < 4 disconnections), no daily charge owed for 2026-10-06 yet, the refund credit itself does not reconnect the meter (only a payment does, and the balance stays below 10.00).

PERSONA. Dwayne is plain-spoken, opens with the surface goal (how much to get the lights back on, pay now by card), gives membership number and phone only when asked, cannot give join date or account number, authorises any posting passively, reacts to a refund or a higher alert only after the agent mentions them, answers how he pays and about Round Up help only if asked, accepts the amount, pays in person through the phone line, closes when the payment is confirmed.

STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers -> verify -> service account -> enrollment -> ledger -> notifications -> meter tests -> refund 14.77 (agent) -> certificates, service payments, arrangements, arrange ledger -> alert reset 61 (agent) -> service charges, capital account and ledger -> member pays 56.8 through the phone payment line (user).

EASY MISTAKES. Quoting on the opening world (balance -7.36, alert 55) gives a different figure; refunding over six months or at the full 3.80 percent; counting the within-tolerance test as fast; taking the full cushion although an Operation Round Up pledge limits it to the fixed charges; using the last month's daily cost for the alert of a short-history account; counting missed installments instead of the default.

POLICY/GT CLOSURE. meter refund -> post_meter_error_refund_29b7beca -> computations[0] step 8 refund_amount; alert reset -> reset_low_balance_alert_c29238fa -> computations[1] step 14 low_balance_alert_amount; restore -> make_restore_payment_2eb3ad28 -> computations[2] step 19 gross_payment_amount. required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies in the same order. Difficulty-level: tasks 0 and 1 together claim all five extended policies and all five tools, pairwise disjoint.

AUDIT ROUND 2 REVISIONS. F-3 (mislabelled method): the pledge factor's tiers now compute the cushion three different ways (waived for a LIHEAP or county pledge; fixed charges only - days x daily_facility_charge - for a Salvation Army or Operation Round Up pledge; days x average daily cost otherwise), renamed assistance_pledge_cushion_method; restore payment recomputed 60.36 -> 56.8, skip effects 71.57 / 50.8. F-4 (incoherent baseline): the refund rule and its baseline now state 'The test-request courtesy and the disconnection courtesy are each zero (courtesy_tests_default and courtesy_disconnects_default).' and the ladders say 'instead' / 'stays at zero'; refund unchanged 14.77. O-3: the earlier within-tolerance test must also precede the fast test (compute binding fast_date). O-2: the patronage rule states that one distribution-margin allocation is booked per patronage year. Observation on alert history: low-balance alert added 2026-09-24. Earlier revision log: the 2026-09-09 payment was lowered to 65.00 so the balance stood at -0.27 before the 2026-09-22 disconnection; the opening alert amount 55.00 equals what the reset rule gives as of 2026-09-22. MANUAL GATES re-checked: both prerequisite sentences negated-direction, record-visible state for the refund, action form with fallback for the reset; the owner=user payment is keyed by the member himself; all writes synchronous.

DIFFICULTY-LEVEL CLOSING (final run after audit round 2, no --task): check_extended EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks REPLAY OK; check_solvability SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute COMPUTE OK; check_grounding GROUNDING OK; check_cache_diff INFO only; check_cross_fire SCOPE OK. check_traceability not run: the KB is not yet published. Union: task 0 {carried-in credit, activation payment}, task 1 {meter refund, alert reset, restore payment} = all five extended policies; no policy or tool shared or reserved.
user_scenario: You are Dwayne Hollis, sixty-three, a retired county road-crew foreman who lives by himself out on Sulphur Lick Road and has been a Cedar Fork member since 1996. You put the house on PrePay Power in August because it was easier than a big bill every month. The power went off yesterday morning and it is still off; you are calling this Tuesday afternoon. You start with something like: "Afternoon, this is Dwayne Hollis out on Sulphur Lick Road. That PrePay shut my power off yesterday morning and I need to know how much it's going to take to get the lights back on. I'll pay it right now with my card." Only when the representative asks you to verify yourself do you give your membership number, 0428843, and your phone number, 2705552906; you don't know the date you joined offhand and you don't carry your account number in your head. You don't know how the cooperative works the amount out and you don't try to; you want a number, you want to pay it on this call, and you want the power back on. If the representative tells you they first need to post a credit or change a setting on your PrePay account, you say that's fine, go ahead. If they tell you a refund came through for your meter, you say "So that meter really was running fast, I figured as much," and you leave it at that. If they tell you your low-balance text will now come at a higher amount, you say that suits you fine. Only if they ask how you usually pay do you say you pay at the kiosk in town, a little at a time. Only if they ask about energy assistance do you say the Operation Round Up people told you they had put in for some help, but you don't know how much or when. When they give you the amount you accept it as it is. You pay it yourself: when the representative hands you the phone payment line, you key in your card and exactly the amount they told you, and you read back the confirmation number if they ask. Once they confirm the payment went through you thank them and hang up.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's member profile by the name he gives.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write needs the member's customer reference number.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Verify the caller with the membership number and phone number he states.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identity must be verified before account information is discussed or anything is changed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the Schedule R service account under the PrePay meter.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Its rate schedule supplies the tolerance, correction limit, tax and power cost adjustment; its id scopes the service-side reads.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the PrePay enrollment: disconnected for low balance, prepaid balance, alert amount, activation date, tier.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The balance, alert amount, activation date and tier enter all three computations.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the enrollment's daily charge lines and payments, and see that no meter error refund is on it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The refund window lines, the alert and cushion daily costs and the payment counts come from these rows; the absence of a refund line shows the restore quote's state is not met.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the enrollment's alerts: three low-balance disconnections in the one-month window.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The disconnection counts set the disconnection courtesy, the warning days, the alert reset owed and the restore target.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the two meter tests: within tolerance on 2026-08-28, fast by 3.80 percent on 2026-10-06.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The fast test makes the refund owed; both tests set the window, the share and the test-request courtesy.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the meter error refund tool named by the refund rule.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Credit the meter error refund for the fast test to the prepaid balance.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The refund is owed for the fast test, and the restore payment is not quoted until the balance carries it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the medical certificate received 2025-11-20 on the service account.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: A certificate in the twelve-month window adds warning days.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the service account's payments: the returned e-check of 2026-05-14 and the Operation Round Up pledge of 2026-10-02.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The return adds warning days; the pledge scales the restore cushion.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the member's payment arrangement.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The arrangement ledger read next needs its reference.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the arrangement ledger: two missed installments and the default rebill of 2025-03-12.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: A default in the twenty-four-month window adds warning days.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the low-balance alert reset tool named by the alert reset rule.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Reset the low-balance alert amount owed after the latest disconnection.
